subject: Re: Data handling, no-train commitment, and EU processing options
messages:
From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@medinformatics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questions on training use and EU residency

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — our security and procurement teams reviewed and have some gating items before procurement can move forward. High level asks: 

- We need a clear, simple no-training (no use for model improvement) commitment for customer data that we can show procurement. Can Redwood commit to not using our content for model training or improvements by default, and if not, what opt-out language would look like?
- Output ownership: our legal team wants explicit language that customer prompts and model outputs are owned/controlled by us and are not used to derive product enhancements without consent.
- Subprocessors and transfers: we need the current subprocessor list and confirmation of EU processing or a data residency option (we process PHI).
- Evidence: can you provide a short SOC 2 Type II summary and any recent attestations that your security team can present to ours?

If it's easier, loop your legal and security folks and we can set up a 30-minute call. Procurement is aiming for a decision by EOW next week, so a quick turnaround would help.

Thanks,
Alyssa Morgan
Sr. Security Program Manager
MedInformatics

Attachment: (none)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@medinformatics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions on training use and EU residency

Hi Alyssa — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front, followed by proposed next steps: 

- No-train: We can offer a contractual no-training commitment for Customer Content (language can be added to the DPA). By default hosted customers are included in our telemetry/ops pipelines, but we will scope an explicit prohibition on using Customer Content to train or improve our model weights if you require that.
- Output/ownership: We can include a clause that Customer retains ownership of prompts and outputs and that Redwood will not assert ownership of customer-generated outputs or use them to create derivative model IP without consent.
- Subprocessors & EU processing: I'm attaching our latest subprocessor csv and a SOC 2 summary. We also offer a Dedicated EU processing option (isolated pool in the eu-central region) and an on-prem/private deployment if you need full control.

Next steps: I'm looping in our Legal (Laura) and Security (Neha) to (1) draft the DPA amendment for a no-train clause and output ownership language, and (2) confirm the scope of evidence we can share. Can you confirm whether MedInformatics requires encryption key separation / BYOK or if the SOC2 summary + subprocessor list will suffice for procurement?

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to resolve any open questions and get a signature path started.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessors_list_2027-04.csv; soc2_type2_summary_2027-04.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MedInformatics - ask re: no-train + output ownership (procurement timeline EOW)

Forwarding Alyssa's note — procurement wants explicit language and evidence this week. Can you help with the redline and evidence package? Key asks from procurement/security: 

1) A clear no-training commitment: proposed plain-language clause below.

2) Output rights: single-sentence guarantee that customer prompts and outputs are customer property and will not be used to generate model-derived IP or training corpora without customer opt-in.

3) Subprocessor and transfer evidence: current list + statement on EU processing / Dedicated EU pool + SOC 2 summary.

Suggested no-train clause (please refine):
"Provider will not use Customer Content (including prompts, requests, and outputs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Provider's models or machine learning systems, nor will Provider include Customer Content in any training, evaluation, or research corpus, except with Customer's explicit written consent."

Laura — can you draft a DPA amendment (redline) that includes the above and a short definition of Customer Content and a representation around ownership of outputs? Neha — can you confirm what evidence we can provide (SOC2 summary, recent pen test, subprocessors list) and whether we can state that Dedicated EU processing is available and that cache retention can be disabled/TTL shortened? Vivek — any operational knobs (BYOK, key separation, ephemeral caches) we should offer here to accelerate?

I need something we can send to Alyssa by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sean

(Quoted original message below)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: MedInformatics - ask re: no-train + output ownership (procurement timeline EOW)

Sean / team — Draft attached: redwood_dpa_amendment_v2.docx. High level summary of changes I put in the draft: 

- No-Train Clause (contractual): "Provider shall not use Customer Content for the purpose of training, tuning, fine-tuning, or otherwise improving Provider's models or machine learning systems. Provider will not include Customer Content in any training, evaluation, or research datasets without Customer's prior written consent."

- Output Ownership: "Customer retains all intellectual property rights in Customer Content and any outputs generated in response to Customer requests. Provider will not claim rights to Customer Content or outputs or use such materials to derive model improvements absent Customer's written consent."

- Subprocessors / Transfers: Added a Section describing subprocessors and a commitment to provide updated lists and data transfer mechanisms (SCCs where applicable) and an option for Dedicated EU processing for customers who require EU residency.

- Evidence: We can attach a SOC 2 Type II summary and provide the full report under NDA. Also offering a short statement: "Redwood operates security, change control, and access controls consistent with SOC 2 controls; summary attached."

Operational options for the customer (to be added as a separate schedule): BYOK (customer-managed keys), Dedicated EU cluster, and reduced cache retention TTLs for sessions. Vivek — please confirm the BYOK and cache TTL wording; Neha please confirm the SOC2 summary that we attach and whether we need a redaction step before sending to external counsel.

Attaching: redwood_dpa_amendment_v2.docx (contains redline + new schedule for processing options).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dpa_amendment_v2.docx
From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa.morgan@medinformatics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Lawton <ben.lawton@acme-legal.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data handling, no-train commitment, and EU processing options

Sean / Laura,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft amendment. Procurement and security reviewed redwood_dpa_amendment_v2.docx and the SOC 2 summary — both look good in principle. A few quick items before procurement signs: 

- We need a one-line certification that Redwood will not use MedInformatics Content to train or improve models (suitable for our purchase order). The clause in the DPA is fine, but procurement prefers a short attestation: "Redwood certifies that it will not use MedInformatics Customer Content to train, tune, or improve any of Redwood's models without explicit written consent from MedInformatics." Can you provide that as a signed letter or an addendum?
- Subprocessors: the list you provided is fine; legal would like a short description of where EU subprocessors process data (region/CCPA/SCCs).
- Timeline: procurement needs the signed DPA amendment + the certification letter by EOW Monday to get the PO processed next week.

If you can get the signed attestation and a short snip about EU subprocessors (region + SCCs) into DocuSign, we'll start the PO. Also please include the Dedicated EU processing option in the schedule for completeness.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Sr. Security Program Manager
MedInformatics
